distribution: GameAnalysis lightweight repository may exclude tools/, but agents should automatically restore trusted third-party tools when needed and persist them under tools/.

tools.name: AssetRipper
tools.purpose: Unity project reconstruction and full local export from user-authorized game folders.

tools.name: UABEA
tools.purpose: Fallback Unity asset bundle inspection when AssetRipper or UnityPy cannot read a specific container.

tools.name: GDRETools
tools.version_check: Godot RE Tools v2.6.0; --gdre-version may return exit code 1, but recovery/list commands must return 0.
tools.purpose: List and recover user-authorized Godot 2.x/3.x/4.x PCK projects, decompile supported GDScript bytecode, and restore imported resources.

tools.name: Godot Engine 3.2.3
tools.version_check: 3.2.3.stable.official; this Windows build may return exit code 255 for --version, so validate hash plus stdout and process cleanup.
tools.purpose: Exact-version secondary static/editor parsing validation for recovered Godot 3.2.3 projects after tool/EditorPlugin/GDNative scanning; never run the game main scene.

tools.name: UnityPy
tools.purpose: Scripted extraction of readable Unity Sprite, Texture2D, TextAsset, AudioClip, and animation-frame data.

tools.name: pytest
tools.purpose: Run GameAnalysis Skill regression tests through scripts/run_skill_tests.ps1 using the bundled Python environment.

tools.name: Pillow
tools.purpose: Validate and fully decode configured image formats with Pillow verify/load before Godot recovered resources are classified and copied.

tools.name: pefile
tools.purpose: Parse PE headers, sections, image base, .pdata runtime functions, and file/RVA mappings for local native-code analysis such as Klei/DST WorldSim binding recovery.

tools.name: capstone
tools.purpose: Disassemble x64 wrapper functions, recover direct call targets, and resolve RIP-relative strings during local native-code analysis.

tools.name: repak
tools.purpose: Read-only Unreal .pak info/list/get workflows for user-authorized packaged games before any optional asset export.

tools.name: UEViewer / UModel
tools.purpose: Optional Unreal package viewer/exporter for small verified samples. Large commercial packages may require engine version parameters or time out; record failures.

tools.name: UndertaleModCli
tools.purpose: Automated local reading and exporter-script execution for user-authorized GameMaker data.win files.

tools.name: UndertaleModTool
tools.purpose: GUI cross-checker and source of bundled GameMaker Resource Exporters scripts such as ExportAllSprites, ExportAllTextures, ExportAllSounds, and ExportAllStringsJSON.

tools.name: ARM ASTC Encoder / astcenc
tools.purpose: Decode Cocos Creator and other mobile ASTC textures to local PNG previews for user-authorized study outputs. This local copy is the official windows-x64 release for x64 Windows; still record URL, version, license, SHA256, and -version/-help output in each current study-root.

tools.name: Stexatlaser / Stex
tools.purpose: Default Klei TEX/KTEX to PNG converter for Don't Starve Together and similar Klei resources.

tools.name: DstAnimTool
tools.local_patch: Python 3 compatibility: write XML as UTF-8 text, decode bytes hash strings, and preserve unknown facing bitmasks as _facing_<hex> suffixes.
tools.purpose: Decompile Klei/DST anim.bin and build.bin files into XML for animation structure analysis.

tools.name: python-fsb5
tools.purpose: Primary FSB5 sample extractor for Klei/DST FMOD banks. The Windows release supplies libogg/libvorbis DLLs needed for Vorbis sample rebuilding.

tools.name: vgmstream CLI
tools.purpose: Decode user-authorized game audio to WAV, including FSB fallback and Wwise external WEM plus every decodable BNK subsong. Metadata probes must use -m -I to prevent the CLI from writing a default WAV beside the input; decodes must always use an explicit -o path.

tools.name: KleiTEXConverter
tools.status: Downloaded but not used by default because this host lacks Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App 5.0.0; Stex is the CLI default.
tools.purpose: GUI/batch fallback for Klei TEX conversion when the required .NET Desktop 5 runtime is available.

tools.name: ktools mirror bundle
tools.license: GPL lineage per nsimplex/ktools; mirror binary provenance should be rechecked before redistribution.
tools.status: krane.exe 4.4.0 is runnable on this host and was verified against a modern Wilson build: it produced a Spriter SCML project with 15 folders and 132 non-empty PNG files, and successfully round-tripped an official scml.exe export. Use an ordinary ASCII isolation root; non-ASCII paths reproduce MagickPNGErrorHandler/WriteBlob failures. ktech.exe remains a separate fallback and is not implied by this krane validation.
tools.safety: Extract ZIP members to an isolated ASCII directory and pass explicit build.bin/anim.bin inputs or their containing directory. Do not pass a broad game root, do not modify game ZIPs, and do not treat an axis-aligned BILD-to-canvas reconstruction as a visual fidelity check for multi-quad frames.
tools.purpose: Decompile a user-authorized Klei Build plus animation Bank into clean per-Symbol PNG files and an editable Spriter SCML seed, then validate official exports by round-trip.

tools.name: BrashMonkey Spriter Essentials
tools.source: User-provided local installation; BrashMonkey Spriter manual documents SCML project authoring
tools.license: External user-installed application; not redistributed by this skill
tools.validation: Opened the generated xuanxiao.scml in the real GUI, showed the xuanxiao entity, 15 resource folders, 12 animations including BUILD_PLAYER, and rendered run_loop_down without shattered strips.
tools.safety: Launch Spriter.exe directly. The local shortcut targets a missing D: path. Never run Spriter_70036_177776.exe from the candidate software folder; audit identified it as a different product (全能电脑助手), not Spriter.
tools.purpose: Edit and visually validate DST-compatible SCML projects before compiling them with Klei's official scml.exe.

tools.name: Klei Don't Starve Mod Tools SCML compiler
tools.version: official source commit 3fe0cad89848c9d0fca8a4139a0491d188497636; local VS2022 v143 Win32 release build
tools.license: MIT for Klei source and binaries; bundled third-party components retain their own licenses

build.compiler: Visual Studio 2022 Community MSBuild / PlatformToolset v143 / Win32 Release

runtime_patch.reason: The upstream Windows Python27 bundle omits python27.dll and VC90 CRT files on this host.

tools.validation: Direct isolated compile of bundled wand.scml returned 0 and produced anim/wand.zip with build.bin, anim.bin and atlas-0.tex; output SHA-256 3D1DBFC71A0E0ACCDA47E26AD4B9B06F990809345E0B7CD696311D3CED8557B2.
tools.safety: Call scml.exe directly with an isolated SCML and mod root. Do not use autocompiler.exe for first-time or broad-root validation because it recursively scans visible mods directories.
tools.purpose: Compile user-authorized Spriter SCML plus transparent part PNGs into a character-owned Klei Build/Anim/Atlas package with compiler-generated pivots, meshes and UVs.

tools.name: Electron gallery viewer template
tools.source: Local template generated from earlier verified gallery viewer workflows.
tools.purpose: Legacy-compatible template for historical HTML gallery workflows; not the default image gallery path. New studies use GameImageGallery with per-project BAT, manifest, thumbnails, and error logs.

tools.name: GameImageGallery
tools.source: Local fixed Electron image gallery built from assets/image-gallery-viewer-src.
tools.license: Internal GameAnalysis tool bundle; Electron runtime follows upstream Electron licensing.
tools.purpose: Open GameAnalysis study-root image manifests through a fixed local Windows EXE. Each project generates only a BAT launcher, manifest, thumbnails, and error logs.

tools.name: GameModelViewer
tools.source: Local Electron/Three.js model viewer built from assets/model-gallery-viewer-src.
tools.license: Local wrapper; Electron MIT; Three.js MIT
tools.purpose: Offline local preview of GameAnalysis exported glTF/GLB/FBX models. Each project generates only a BAT launcher, manifest, thumbs, preview-cache, and error logs.

tools.name: GameVfxViewer
tools.source: Local fixed Electron Unity VFX viewer built from assets/vfx-viewer-src.
tools.license: Local wrapper; Electron runtime follows upstream Electron licensing.
tools.purpose: Offline local preview of GameAnalysis Unity VFX manifests and best-effort reconstructed ParticleSystem, TrailRenderer, and LineRenderer data. Supports machine-readable UTF-8 self-test evidence through --self-test-output. Each project generates only a BAT launcher, manifest, reconstructed JSON, preview-cache, unity-export, and error/status records.

tools.name: GameCharacterAnimationViewer
tools.license: MIT; copied beside the installed executable
tools.purpose: Character-first Don't Starve Together animation browsing and live playback from the installed game root; independent of the legacy GameAnimationViewer Bank manifest.

tools.name: GameAnimationViewer
tools.source: Local fixed Electron animation viewer built from assets/game-animation-viewer-src.
tools.license: Local wrapper; Electron runtime follows upstream Electron licensing.
tools.purpose: Offline local preview and export of real rendered GameAnalysis animation frames from manifest-authorized source roots. Supports machine-readable UTF-8 self-test evidence through --self-test-output; project study roots receive only launchers, preview caches, exports, and status records.

tools.name: ILSpy / ilspycmd
tools.purpose: Check whether a Unity Assembly-CSharp.dll contains real managed IL method bodies or only dummy/stub signatures.

tools.name: Il2CppDumper
tools.purpose: Generate dump.cs, script.json, il2cpp.h, stringliteral.json, and DummyDll from GameAssembly.dll plus global-metadata.dat.

tools.name: Cpp2IL
tools.purpose: Optional IL2CPP analysis fallback. It may fail on newer metadata versions; record the failure instead of replacing Il2CppDumper.

tools.name: Ghidra
tools.version_check: Headless usage banner is available when JAVA_HOME points to tools/JDK21; this build does not support a standalone -version flag.
tools.purpose: Analyze native code for Unity GameAssembly.dll, Klei/DST WorldSim PE functions, and other user-authorized local binaries; use targeted decompile CSVs instead of broad source dumps.

tools.name: JDK
tools.purpose: Portable Java runtime used by bundled Ghidra without changing the system Java installation.

tools.name: IDA / IDA Free
tools.purpose: Optional manual cross-check for native code. IDA Free is not the default automated route because licensing and automation capabilities are limited.

boundary: These entries describe expected local paths and trusted sources for user-authorized learning workflows. The public repository may omit tools/; when network is available, missing tools must be restored automatically from trusted sources with license checks, source URL, version, hash, and help/version output, then persisted under tools/. Do not use them to distribute third-party original assets.
